clue.text: Demonic, nasty American — one needing to be born again

definitions.text: one needing to be born again

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned ugly and mangled, so the letters of the first word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wicked, unpleasant American is told he needs spiritual rebirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' signals the anagram. In John's Gospel, Jesus tells the Pharisee who visits him by night that a man must be born again.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel of John this Pharisee is told by Jesus that he must be reborn to see the kingdom of God.

clue.text: I'm prickly enemy, one may conjecture

parts.note: an enemy is, one might guess, nobody's friend: 'no' as in not one
a pal is a friend, which an enemy is not

explanation.surface: A thorny foe introduces itself while others speculate about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one may conjecture' flags the loose reasoning that an enemy is 'no pal'. The definition is spoken by the plant itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Mexican prickly-pear cactus, so it could fairly describe itself as prickly.

clue.text: House as prison harbouring abused tot

indicators.note: harbouring means holding within, so one piece shelters the other inside it

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or twisted, signalling that the little word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A home serving as a jail where a child is mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' signals the anagram of the child, and 'harbouring' shuts it inside the prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically in the country.

clue.text: Finish with one of the honours — the last trump?

parts.note: to do someone, or do for them, is to finish them off
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Ending a game holding an honour card, with a final trump to play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests bridge, with honours and trumps; in fact the last trump is the trumpet call heralding the Day of Judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom is the Last Judgement, which the last trumpet announces, so the question mark marks a definition by association.

clue.text: Prominent lefty, one of the brothers?

definitions.meaning: Karl, the famous left-wing political philosopher who wrote Das Kapital
Groucho, Chico, Harpo and the others were the comedy brothers of that surname

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the father of communism and to the American comedy brothers.

clue.text: Posh maybe to have a look at purchasing options

definitions.text: have a look at purchasing options

parts.note: the word Posh is the letters of shop moved round, so it is an example of a shop rearranged

explanation.surface: Victoria Beckham, known as Posh, browsing for something to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: POSH is SHOP with its letters shifted 'around'; 'maybe' marks it as one such example. Posh Spice, Victoria Beckham, is famous for shopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop around is to compare prices and options at several sellers before buying.

clue.text: Competes, having got hold of second-rate instrument

indicators.note: having got hold of means gripping, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: vies means competes
B is a grade below A, hence second-rate

explanation.surface: A player contends while stuck with a poor-quality instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibes is the informal name for the vibraphone, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Rail union in grip of malicious person and troublemaker

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a viper is a spiteful, treacherous person
TU is the abbreviation for trade union
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A railway union caught up with a spiteful agitator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like the railway, but it is the verb meaning to complain bitterly. Ate, the Greek goddess of mischief, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to scold abusively, which is to berate or revile with harsh words.

clue.text: Like algebra? We don't like that — unproductive!

parts.note: boo is the cry of disapproval
a lean year is a poor, unproductive one

explanation.surface: Someone groans at algebra as a fruitless subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Boolean algebra, named after George Boole, works with true and false values in logic.

clue.text: Smooth way to embrace cold fish

parts.note: to sand is to smooth a surface

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug or enclose, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A suave approach to hugging a chilly fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small eel-like fish that burrows in sand, also called sand eel.

clue.text: Object to accelerate?

definitions.meaning: to object firmly, refusing to allow something
to speed up, by pressing the car's pedal hard

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to take a firm stand against something and to press the accelerator pedal.

clue.text: What's used for writing in space between lines of print

definitions.meaning: the graphite core of a pencil
in typesetting, the strip of metal used to space out lines of type

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names pencil graphite and, pronounced 'led', the metal spacing between printed lines.

clue.text: Scot could rouse the holidaymakers maybe?

parts.note: a holiday camp full of holidaymakers is the camp
a bell is rung to wake people

explanation.surface: A Scotsman who might wake everyone on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase: a bell to wake the camp, as at a British holiday camp of the Butlin's kind.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the surname of a famous Scottish clan, so a person bearing it is a Scot.

clue.text: Form of communication when people are lying?

definitions.text: Form of communication when people are lying?

parts.words: Form of communication when people are lying?
parts.note: lying suggests telling untruths, but here it means lying down in bed, where intimate chat happens

explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names the intimate conversation a couple share in bed.

clue.text: Tough, yet yellow at heart?

definitions.meaning: hard-headed and unsentimental, like a cynical detective
describes an egg cooked solid, its yolk yellow at the centre

explanation.definitionFit: The term means callous and tough, and also describes an egg cooked until set, with a yellow centre.

clue.text: Those people fuss about one king, making a show

parts.note: them means those people
I is the Roman numeral one
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
ado is fuss

explanation.surface: People make a fuss over a monarch, putting on a spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has ADO round I and K.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera is a stage show.

clue.text: Bitter tears splashing — they are salty

parts.note: tart means sharp or bitter in taste

indicators.note: splashing suggests liquid scattered about, so the letters of the word are scattered

explanation.surface: Sour tears flowing and tasting of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartrates are salts of tartaric acid, so they are things of a salt kind.

clue.text: Fight knight in eg dilapidated castle

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a ruin, such as a crumbling castle
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight battling in a crumbling fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is a quarrel or confrontation.

clue.text: Beast subsequently switching sides

indicators.note: the sides are L and R, left and right, which swap places

parts.note: later means subsequently

explanation.surface: An animal that changes allegiance afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching sides' swaps L (left) and R (right) in LATER, giving RATEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian animal.

clue.text: Bit of mosaic shows girl entertaining monarch

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one piece takes the other in

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A girl puts up a king or queen in a piece of mosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a crossword convention for the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or pieces used to make a mosaic.

clue.text: Town liable to fall apart when led by duke

indicators.note: led by means coming after, so the duke piece goes first

parts.note: unstable means liable to collapse

explanation.surface: A shaky place headed by a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, England.

clue.text: Skirt said to be suitable for one sort of schoolgirl?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word sounds like the one given

parts.note: to skirt is to border, to edge round

explanation.surface: A dress described as fit for a particular girl at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning to border.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is a pupil who lives at the school during term.

clue.text: Material for furniture brings woe with doors getting warped

indicators.note: warped means twisted out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Warped doors make for misery in a furniture-maker's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewood is a dark, fragrant hardwood prized in cabinet-making.

clue.text: Fish hook

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of the carp family
the backward-pointing point of a fish-hook or arrow

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a carp-like fish and the backward point on a hook.

clue.text: Scientist gets change out of liquid state reported

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word sounds like the one given

parts.note: to boil is to turn from liquid into vapour

explanation.surface: A researcher heats a liquid to vapour, according to accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Boyle, the 17th-century chemist, gave his name to Boyle's law of gases.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Boyle was an Anglo-Irish chemist and physicist.

clue.text: Good bunch of students? Beasts!

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students, a British body

explanation.surface: Praise for a group of students, followed by an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus are wildebeest, large African antelopes.

clue.text: Good fortune not half needed with party game

indicators.note: not half means losing half of the word's letters, here its back half

parts.note: luck is good fortune
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Luck is needed in some party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops the second half of LUCK to leave LU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Paper unashamedly into being perverse?

indicators.note: perverse means contrary and twisted, so the letters are put in a twisted order

explanation.surface: A newspaper that brazenly indulges in kinkiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being perverse' rearranges UNASHAMEDLY and INTO. The Mail on Sunday is a British Sunday tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mail on Sunday is a British Sunday newspaper.

clue.text: Prime thing for sale — rubbishy stuff that's piled high?

indicators.note: the prime thing of a word is its first letter

parts.note: tack is cheap, tacky goods

explanation.surface: A top bargain on sale among the junk heaped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime thing for' takes the first letter of 'sale'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stack is a heap, something piled high.

clue.text: Party broadcast sure to be a sermon?

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A political party broadcast certain to be preachy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party broadcast' looks like a political TV slot, but the party is a dance and 'broadcast' scrambles the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a formal talk or lecture, of which a sermon is one kind.
